summary: The revised plan closes the earlier SQL-template and PostgreSQL privilege-test gaps, and no embedded secret values were found in the supplied feature artifacts. Two in-scope blockers remain: ordinary same-PG19 archives appended across the pgcenter upgrade are not replay-safe, and the XID-mutating wraparound fixture is still unsafe for the shared integration cluster. Terminal-control sanitisation and acceptance-evidence secret handling also need explicit treatment. A separate pre-existing malformed-archive crash is recorded out of scope.

findings.title: Same-PG19 archives appended across the pgcenter upgrade still fail or render with stale layout state
findings.description: The plan recognises that record -a can pair an old pgcenter's 19-column tables row (or 6-column indexes row) with the feature's 20-column (or 7-column) row while both samples declare PostgreSQL 19, but it only adds a DiffIntvl bounds invariant and tests the different PostgreSQL 18-to-19 transition. That transition takes the versionChanged reset branch; the new same-server-version transition does not. The narrow-to-wide diff happens to stay in bounds, but formatStatSample keeps Aligned=true and the old ColsWidth/Cols. A non-empty trailing stats_age then reads missing width 19 (or 6) as zero and aborts with 'zero or negative width, skip'; an empty trailing value can instead be omitted without recomputing the header. Thus an ordinary upgrade followed by record -a produces a broken or misleading report. The CLI currently prints processing errors without propagating a failure from doReport, so automation can also treat the damaged report as successful. Attack/accident vector: a user records PG19 before upgrading, appends after upgrading, and replays tables or indexes; no malformed archive is required. The proposed bounds test cannot detect this render-path failure.
findings.evidence: Source inspection confirmed versionChanged compares only metadata.version and is the sole branch that clears Aligned; formatStatSample returns immediately whenever Aligned is true. The existing Test_app_doReport_errorPathDoesNotHang explicitly builds a same-version narrow-to-wide archive and documents the missing-width error. Read-only command `go test ./report -run 'Test_processData|Test_app_doReport' -count=1 -v` passed, including that error-path test and the three version-change tests; this confirms the tested behavior is an error drain, not successful mixed-width rendering. The planned 180000-to-190000 fixtures cannot cover the same-190000 case.
findings.recommendation: Handle layout changes independently of PostgreSQL-version changes. Before diffing, compare the previous and current column names/width (not merely Ncols metadata); on any change, replace prevStat, clear Aligned and stale Cols/ColsWidth, reset header/sort state, and continue without diffing incompatible layouts. Keep the DiffIntvl invariant as defence in depth, not as the fix. Add same-version 190000 replay tests for both tables and indexes with two old-layout ticks followed by two new-layout ticks, non-empty stats_age, requested sort columns, and both width-change directions; assert successful output, new headers/widths, and no cross-layout delta. Also test blank stats_age so silent omission cannot pass. Correct the unconditional 'Recorded archives: unaffected' compatibility claim until this is implemented.

findings.category: A05 - destructive shared fixture and incomplete cleanup
findings.title: The wraparound fixture still combines cluster-global mutation, irreversible XID consumption, and non-isolated cleanup
findings.description: The revised text says XID consumption is restricted to disposable PG19 fixtures, yet the operative integration-test bullet explicitly disables autovacuum with ALTER SYSTEM on a cluster shared by concurrently running packages. t.Cleanup improves ordinary assertion-failure handling but does not make ALTER SYSTEM interruption-safe, does not define restoration of the original value or verification, and does not clean up the probe relation/procedure. A killed test process can therefore leave persistent autovacuum configuration changed; concurrent tests can observe the disabled launcher and altered transaction ages. Repeated runs leave the probe unless additional cleanup is implemented and monotonically consume XIDs. In addition, autovacuum=off does not suppress emergency wraparound vacuum in all states; the plan now mentions the global threshold but does not require a runtime safety-margin assertion. Attack/accident vector: a normal CI timeout, SIGKILL, runner loss, or overlapping package test during the fixture leaves or observes degraded cluster state, invalidating later tests and potentially causing unexpected vacuum/XID behaviour on a long-lived fixture cluster.
findings.evidence: Read-only source inspection shows NewTestConnectVersion maps every caller for version 190000 to the same 127.0.0.1:21919 pgcenter_fixtures cluster. Callers exist outside internal/query, including Test_collectOverviewStat in internal/stat, so package-parallel go test execution can share this state. The preparation script creates persistent clusters and appends configuration; it is not per-test disposal. Grep of the current feature artifacts found t.Cleanup only for autovacuum restoration and no DROP TABLE/procedure cleanup contract, original-value capture, post-restore SHOW assertion, or cross-package exclusion mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Run this test only in a dedicated single-use PG19 cluster whose destruction is owned by an external harness, so even SIGKILL cannot leave shared state behind; this is the preferred fix. If shared-cluster execution is unavoidable, enforce cross-package exclusion, capture and restore the exact prior effective autovacuum setting with reload in an immediately registered cleanup, verify restoration with SHOW, and add external timeout/trap cleanup. Register cleanup for a feature-unique probe and burn procedure, start each run from a clean state, and assert presence by the probe's reltoastrelid rather than a global row count. Before disabling autovacuum, assert oldest datfrozenxid age is safely below the global autovacuum_freeze_max_age. Keep the irreversible-XID warning and reject execution against non-disposable clusters.

findings.title: The new relation column adds another unsanitised server-to-terminal path
findings.description: The new query intentionally concatenates schemaname and relname from the server and sends relation to the existing cell renderer. printDataCell writes the resulting bytes directly, without removing ESC, C0/C1 controls, OSC sequences, or newlines. A database principal able to create a quoted identifier containing control characters and generate relation statistics can cause that name to appear on autovacuum_scores when a DBA opens the screen; enough dead tuples can make the row prominent. Depending on the terminal emulator, the payload can spoof displayed output, alter terminal state, or request clipboard operations. Pausing extends the display lifetime. This is an existing registered weakness on other screens, not a claim that every terminal executes commands, but the feature adds a new reachable surface and the current plan neither mitigates it nor carries forward the earlier recommendation to update debt [029].
findings.evidence: Source inspection traces relation from PostgreSQL identifiers to `value := s.Result.Values[rownum][i].String` and then `fmt.Fprintf(w, "%-*s", ..., value)` with no sanitisation. Existing printDataCell tests cover truncation and widths, not control-byte removal. Read-only command `go test ./top -run Test_printDataCell_truncatedCellExactBytes -count=1 -v` passed, confirming the exercised printer path; no terminal-emulator exploit was attempted, so emulator-specific consequences remain dependent on the emulator.
findings.recommendation: Sanitise server-controlled cell text at the shared TUI render boundary before width calculation/truncation: remove or visibly encode ESC, C0/C1 controls, and embedded line breaks while preserving valid Unicode. Apply equivalent output encoding to report when stdout is a terminal. Add tests using quoted relation names containing CSI, OSC, newline, and carriage-return payloads and assert no raw control bytes reach the writer. If the project deliberately defers the shared fix, explicitly accept the new exposure in the spec and add autovacuum_scores to debt [029], rather than silently dropping the prior audit recommendation.

findings.category: A09 - sensitive data in acceptance evidence
findings.title: Planned acceptance evidence has no no-secret, redaction, or raw-archive handling contract
findings.description: SC-1 records a full pgcenter archive and the plan requires retained base/freeze/final evidence, but says nothing about acceptable evidence contents. Full recording includes activity and pg_stat_statements query text as well as client/application metadata; record's default string limit is unlimited. Query text can contain authentication DDL, connection details, application tokens, or other sensitive literals even when the displayed tables/indexes reports do not. Raw tmux captures and traced setup commands create additional disclosure paths. Accident vector: an executor reuses a stand or runs setup SQL containing sensitive values, then retains or publishes the tar, command transcript, or capture as feature evidence readable by a wider audience. No actual secret value was found in the supplied artifacts; this finding concerns the missing preventive contract.
findings.evidence: Read-only inspection shows tarRecorder.collect executes every filtered view and write stores complete PGresult JSON, while the activity/statements SELECT lists include query text. The record CLI default is strlimit=0 (no limit). Searches of the current tech spec found evidence-retention requirements but no redaction, secret scan, no-secret fixture, raw-artifact exclusion, or publication restriction. A credential-pattern search over the feature directory returned no matches, so no secret is reproduced in this report.
findings.recommendation: Make SC-1 use a newly created, synthetic, explicitly no-secret database and fixture workload. Do not attach or commit raw full archives or unreviewed terminal/session transcripts; retain only the tar member listing, hashes, and sanitised tables/indexes output needed for the assertions. Define a pre-publication redaction/secret-scan gate for commands, environment output, SQL text, hostnames, and captures, with restrictive local permissions and deletion of raw temporary artifacts. Do not treat --strlimit as a redactor. Require equivalent handling for manual SC-5-SC-8 evidence and prohibit credential values in command transcripts.

findings.category: CWE-20/CWE-129 - malformed recorded archive denial of service
findings.title: Archive-controlled Ncols remains unvalidated and can drive out-of-range indexing
findings.description: Recorded archives are explicitly treated as untrusted input, but PGresult.validate checks row widths against len(Cols) and Nrows against the number of rows without checking Ncols against len(Cols). A crafted archive can declare a much larger Ncols while providing internally consistent Cols and Values. On a diffed report, calculateDelta reaches diff, whose loop uses curr.Ncols and indexes curr.Values and prev.Values with that attacker-controlled bound, causing an index-out-of-range panic. The existing per-entry size cap does not prevent this small-payload crash. Attack vector: convince an operator to run pgcenter report on a downloaded or replaced tar. This vulnerability predates feature 018 and is already reachable on tables/indexes, so it is out of scope for the feature, but the feature's valid-fixture replay tests do not mitigate it.
findings.evidence: Read-only source inspection confirms validate has no Ncols==len(Cols) check and diff loops `l < curr.Ncols` before indexing row slices. Existing TestPGresult_validate covers row-width and Nrows mismatches only. The project's debt [020] records prior reproduction with an archive declaring Ncols far above its real row width. NewPGresultFile's negative/oversized-entry checks were also inspected; they bound allocation size but do not validate this semantic shape. No new crash test was run because the class is already documented as reproduced and this audit did not alter source fixtures.
findings.recommendation: Track this separately as a security fix: reject negative or implausible Ncols/Nrows, require Ncols==len(Cols), enforce row-width and consumer index bounds, and reject incompatible adjacent layouts before diffing. Add malformed-archive tests for Ncols larger/smaller than Cols, empty columns with rows, invalid UniqueKey/OrderKey, and mismatched same-version layouts. Return a descriptive report error rather than panicking; do not rely on entry-size limits or valid synthetic replay fixtures as proof of untrusted-input safety.
